clues: This city is the far north capital of a land in the north of Europe. It stands on the shore of a wide gulf, with the cold sea to its south.
In deep winter, the day here lasts less than six hours, and the sun stays very low. In summer, the day stretches to near nineteen hours of light.
In 1812, an emperor moved the seat of rule to this town from an older town in the west. He wanted less sway from Sweden and a seat closer to his own capital.
Work began in 1748 on a great sea fort near this city, the largest sea fort in Europe in its day. The fort raised the standing of the whole town.
The work of state for Finland runs from this city. It is the chief hub of the land for rule, schools, banks, and arts.
